newsitem.title: UK: British Gas, HFC Bank launch credit card.
newsitem.headline: British Gas, HFC Bank launch credit card.

text.p: British Gas Plc and HFC Bank on Wednesday said they are jointly launching a credit card named Goldfish, which will be used as a platform to introduce additional financial services products under the Goldfish name.
British Gas and HFC, a subsidiary of Household International Inc, said they formed a 50-50 joint venture, Goldbrand Development Ltd, to their launch financial services products.
The Goldfish credit card will be available primarily as a MasterCard, but will also be issued as a Visa card.
British Gas said the Goldfish venture marks its first major diversification beyond its core business.
The Goldfish credit card is being introduced with a 10 million stg marketing campaign, including television and print press advertising and direct mail promotions.

The credit card will carry no annual fee, an annual interest rate of 18.9 percent, and will offer redemption points for each pound charged. Points initially can be redeemed against British Gas bills, but Goldbrand said it plans to introduce additional redemption partners, such as major retailers and grocers.
"Right from day one, Goldfish is going to take on established players in financial services," Goldbrand managing director Michael Parsons told a news conference.
Goldbrand declined to detail how many credit cards it expects to issue.
"We have very ambitious targets," said Martin Rutland, a spokesman for Goldbrand. "We want to challenge the market leader."
Parsons said the card is designed to appeal to a very broad segment of the market, including adults who have never previously owned a credit card.
British Gas selected HFC as its partner due to HFC's expertise in marketing credit cards. Household International is the second-largest issuer of MasterCards on a worldwide basis.
Parsons admitted that the Goldfish card draws heavily on features that have been introduced in the U.S. credit card market, including the absence of an annual fee and the redemption point scheme.
Parsons declined to say when the credit card is expected to reach break even, but said profitability is not the only goal.
"Our focus unlike the High Street banks is not simply a profit," Parsons told Reuters following the news conference. "We want to bring in a number of other products."
But he said that Goldbrand hopes that the credit card will "establish a position in the top three cards fairly quickly."
The top three credit card issuers in the UK currently are Barclays, Lloyds-TSB and National Westminster.
